result.stdout:
SpDev — step through SQL Server stored procedures.

Usage:
  spdev-cli run <file.sql> [options]       Execute with tracing
  spdev-cli profile <file.sql> [options]   Measure every statement and analyze actual plans (SpDev Pro)
  spdev-cli benchmark <file.sql> [options] Profile several runs and compare them (SpDev Pro)
  spdev-cli describe <file.sql>            Print the procedure's parameters as JSON
  spdev-cli instrument <file.sql>          Print the instrumented SQL (diagnostics)

Run options:
  -c, --connection <string>   Connection string (default: SPDEV_CONNECTION_STRING env var)
  -p, --param <name=value>    Parameter value; repeatable. Use name=NULL for SQL NULL.
      --params-json <json>    Parameters as a JSON object ({"CustomerId": "5", "Note": null})
  -s, --search-dir <dir>      Extra directory to search for called procedures; repeatable
      --no-nested             Call database versions of nested procedures (no local files)
      --no-trace              Run the local code without taking snapshots
      --max-steps <n>         Snapshot limit per procedure call (default 20000)
      --max-rows <n>          Rows reported per result set (default 500)
      --timeout <seconds>     Command timeout (default 0 = none)
      --host <auto|temp|database>
                              Where instrumented procedures are created (default auto: #temp
                              procedures unless user-defined types or a non-dbo schema need the database)
      --json                  Write machine-readable NDJSON events to stdout

SpDev Pro options (profile, benchmark; --sandbox also for run):
      --sandbox               Run inside a transaction that is rolled back at the end
      --no-plans              Don't capture actual execution plans
      --plans-dir <dir>       Write the captured plans there as .sqlplan files
      --plan-budget <n>       Plans captured per statement (default 2)
      --repeat <n>            benchmark: number of runs (default 5)
